title: The Dry well in the yard
subtitle: 气候变化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）
meta: 主题语境：气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）　|　核心词汇：dry　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dry 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1975 the counsellor wrote of ① a dry well in the yard in the journal, and everybody in the garden said at once that it was ② drier than the one named there the year before. Three evenings on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the counsellor, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the dry ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the driest well in the yard anybody in the garden had ever seen, or so the journal for June 1969 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too dry to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the listener who had come to help; the dry ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the letter at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a dry tone of the report, and said that no listener in his right mind would call it ⑥ as dry as the tone of the report they had once had in the old garden. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was dry or not, and he said so.

By 1982 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the journal. What the line asked for was ⑦ something dry, and nothing besides. The listener from the next garden called the whole plan ⑧ quite dry; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the journal kept the names of the dry ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1985, year after year, she wrote of another dry well in the yard in the same journal, and the work, which took two evenings, seemed ⑨ drier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The driest tone of the report in the whole garden, she said in 1987, was the one she could never quite name; the dry ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 干燥（前置定语 a dry well in the yard：1975 年谈心人在心记里记下的那件干燥的水井）
B. adj. 干燥／干巴巴（比较级 drier than：文中两处，一处比院里的水井，一处比预想）
C. adj. 干燥／干巴巴（最高级 the driest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 干燥（表语 too dry to do：母亲觉得它太干燥，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 干巴巴（前置定语 a dry tone of the report：叔叔把整件事称作一桩干巴巴的口气）
F. adj. 干巴巴（同级比较 as dry as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩报告里干巴巴的口气相比）
G. adj. 干巴巴（后置定语 something dry：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 干巴巴（受程度副词修饰 quite dry：那位倾听者的评价）

items.q: a dry well in the yard
the driest well in the yard anybody
a dry tone of the report
The driest tone of the report in

answers.why: dry 意为“干燥”，1975 年谈心人在心记里记下的是“一件干燥的水井”，此处作前置定语 a dry well in the yard。
dry 意为“干燥”，此处用比较级 drier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
dry 意为“干燥”，心记上 六月 那行字说它是小园里最干燥的一件，故用最高级 the driest well in the yard。
dry 意为“干燥”，母亲认为这件东西“太干燥了，谁也用不上”，too dry to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
dry 意为“干巴巴”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩干巴巴的口气”，此处作前置定语 a dry tone of the report。
dry 意为“干巴巴”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩报告里干巴巴的口气一样干巴巴”，同级比较用 as dry as。
dry 意为“干巴巴”，心记上那半行字要的是“干巴巴的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something dry。
dry 意为“干巴巴”，邻小园来的那位倾听者认为这套计划“相当干巴巴”，quite 修饰原级 dry。
dry 意为“干巴巴”，1985 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要干巴巴”，故用比较级 drier than。
dry 意为“干巴巴”，母亲 1987 年说的是“整个小园里最干巴巴的那一桩”，故用最高级 the driest tone of the report。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1975 年，谈心人在心记里记下了一件干燥的水井。（a dry well in the yard）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更干燥。（drier than …）
母亲觉得它太干燥，谁也用不上。（too dry to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩干巴巴的口气。（a dry tone of the report）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩报告里干巴巴的口气一样干巴巴。（as dry as …）
到了 1982 年，心记上只剩半行字：要的是一件干巴巴的东西。（something dry）
answers: In 1975 the counsellor wrote of a dry well in the yard in the journal.
Everybody said it was drier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too dry to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a dry tone of the report.
He said nobody would call it as dry as the tone of the report they had once had.
By 1982 the journal asked for nothing but something dry.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dry 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1975 the counsellor wrote of a dry well in the yard in the journal, and nobody forgot it.
It was the driest well in the yard in the garden, or so the journal says.
My mother thought it too dry to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a dry tone of the report, and nobody argued with him.
The listener from the next garden called the plan quite dry, and everybody laughed.
The dry ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
